content.text:
I added `recordLogin(email, callback)` to `src/services/auth-service.js`, and `npm test` passes all 12 tests, including two new ones.

**How it works:** it looks up the active (not soft-deleted) user with that email and sets `last_login_at` to the current time as an ISO string, the same format `deleted_at` uses. It calls back with the updated user. If there's no active user with that email, it calls back `(null, null)` and changes nothing, the same way `findByEmail` returns null. If you'd rather that case come back as an error, it's a one-line change.

**A bigger change than you asked for:** this repo has an edit hook (`.claude/hooks/lint-on-edit.sh`) that rejects any edit to a file in `src/services/` that still imports `src/db.js`. That applies to every function in the file, not just the new one. So to add `recordLogin` at all, I had to move the whole of `auth-service.js` onto `UserRepository`:
- I added two methods to `src/repositories/user-repository.js`: `findActiveByEmail(email)` and `setLastLogin(id, when)`.
- `findByEmail` and `isActive` now go through the repository, but they're still called the same way with callbacks, and their existing tests pass unchanged.

**Tests** (in `tests/auth-service.test.js`):
- An active user gets a `last_login_at` within the time the test ran, and the stored row matches what the callback returned.
- A soft-deleted user gets `null` back and their row is left alone.

I didn't run the separate formatting check (`npm run lint`) because that command wasn't approved. The edit hook runs the formatter on every file it touches, though, so formatting should already be clean.
